mythologySignificance:
Murugan married Deivanai here after Surapadma battle in tradition; cave sanctum and hill sunset draw constant worship.

Classical pilgrimage teaching places Thiruparankundram Murugan Temple within India’s tirtha network: a location where devotion to Lord Murugan (Subramanya) is believed to ripen vows more readily than in ordinary space. Epic, Puranic, and regional mahatmya literature — not a single uniform text — sustain this sense of sacred geography.
localBeliefs:
In popular pilgrimage memory, Thiruparankundram Murugan Temple is especially associated with Rock-cut Murugan · Arupadai Veedu search. Guides and elders retell this identity to first-time visitors as the living ‘reason’ the tirtha draws crowds.

Local sthala-purana and priestly teaching at Thiruparankundram Murugan Temple elaborate how Lord Murugan (Subramanya) blesses devotees who arrive with vows, gratitude, or grief. Festival days intensify these beliefs through processions, special alankara, and community feeding where practised.

Pilgrims commonly link practical customs — dress, queue, prasadam, and parikrama — with spiritual fruit. Such customs are living belief: they vary by region and should be followed as posted by the temple trust or endowment board.
